hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Federal Bank as a granularly funded, Kerala-headquartered private bank with a dominant NRI remittance franchise, scaling profitability by shifting mix toward secured higher-yielding retail assets (gold, LAP, cards) while keeping 85% of deposits in CASA + sub-₹3 Cr tickets.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Granular funding is the stated core of the liability franchise: 'CASA + Deposits < 3Cr' is 85% of total deposits in Q1 FY27, up from 82% in Q1 FY26, with the deck framing deposits as 'up 11% YoY with granular funding at 85% of the book'.
- Remittance market share of 20.34% in FY26 (19.30% FY23, 18.67% FY24, 18.42% FY25), computed by the bank on its own remittances data against preliminary RBI balance-of-payments data; NRE deposits ₹95,710 Cr and NR deposits ₹1,05,123 Cr as of Q1 FY27.
- Retail + SME is held at roughly three-fifths of the book — '(Retail + SME)/Net Advances' at 60.2% in Q1 FY27 (60.9% Q1 FY26), where Retail includes Housing, LAP, Auto, PL, CC & Other Retail and SME includes BuB & CoB.
- Improving granularity on both sides of the balance sheet: Top 20 Borrowers down to 5.4% and Top 20 Depositors to 4.55% of portfolio in Q1FY27, versus 10.03% and 7.09% respectively in Q1FY25.
- Deck labels Q1 FY27 GNPA of 1.52% as 'Highest Ever*' / Net NPA 0.18% as 'Decadal Best' (asterisk: excluding one-off), with sequential comparisons presented on a BAU basis excluding the Q4 FY26 one-off.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Capital position framed as self-funding: 'CRAR at 16.97% and Tier-I at 15.89%, supporting growth with no near-term capital requirement', with Tier-I capital up ₹1,588 Cr on internal accrual funding a 4.5% increase in risk-weighted assets.
- Total capital funds ₹41,015 Cr at Jun-26 versus ₹39,862 Cr at Mar-26; Tier-II fell to ₹2,612 Cr (1.08%) from ₹3,047 Cr (1.32%).
- Balance sheet at ₹3.93 Lakh Cr, with borrowings reduced to ₹18,166 Cr at Jun-26 from ₹21,159 Cr at Mar-26 while deposits rose to ₹3,20,118 Cr; share warrants subscription of ₹1,549 Cr stands unchanged on the liability side.
- Provision coverage strengthened to 87.37% (excluding technical write-offs) from 74.41% a year earlier; Q1 provisions of ₹317 Cr comprised loan loss ₹274 Cr and standard accounts ₹43 Cr.
- No dividend or buyback policy is disclosed in the deck.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [International rating] S&P Global Ratings has assigned the bank its inaugural international issuer credit ratings of BBB-/Stable long-term and A-3 short-term; domestic ratings are AAA on Fixed Deposit, A1+ on Fixed Deposit (short term) and Certificate of Deposit, and IND AA+/CARE AA+ on Tier 2 capital bonds and infrastructure bonds.
- [Group companies] Fedbank Financial Services is a 60.7% subsidiary marketing retail asset products of the bank; Federal Operations & Services (FedServ) is a 100% subsidiary providing operational and technology services from Bangalore, Visakhapatnam, Indore and Kochi; Ageas Federal Life Insurance is a 30% associate JV selling since March 2008.
- [Subsidiary performance] Fedbank Financial Services Q1 FY27: AUM up 34.7% YoY to ₹21,136 Cr, disbursals ₹6,760 Cr (+13.9% YoY), RoA 2.6% and RoE 15.4%, 757 branches across 17 states/UTs, capital adequacy 20.7%, 99.2% of AUM secured, credit cost 0.8%, GNPA 1.6% and NNPA 1.0%.
- [One-off adjustment] The deck repeatedly flags a one-off in Q4 FY26; sequential comparisons and growth metrics are presented on a BAU basis with comparatives adjusted, and several ratio series are marked '(Excl one off)' or '#Excluding one-offs'.
- [Reporting inconsistency] The Net NPA % series differs between slides for Q4 FY26 — the credit-metrics chart shows 0.37 (marked '^Excluding one-offs') while the Key Indicators appendix table shows 0.20.
